I nearly rejected this on my own search error and record the correction. V.3's visible opening only says 'Use Suslin's convention for the integral K_3 comparison', and a grep for 'CGZ' in V.3 returns nothing, which looked like the finding attributing to V.3 something it does not plan. V.3's full text settles it: 'Separately construct the conventions used by Bloch, Goncharov and Calegari-Garoufalidis-Zagier. Prove the comparison maps, their exact small torsion corrections and their rational identifications. Do not erase 2- or 3-torsion merely because the real dilogarithm kills it.' V.3 spells out the names that HB.1 abbreviates. Both stages therefore plan the CGZ/Suslin comparison with its small-torsion corrections. One refinement: V.3 is an ancestor of HB.1, so the fix is for HB.1 to import V.3's comparison rather than for the programme to choose between two owners.

A literal reading of 'admissible nonzero, nonunit field elements' does describe the empty set, since every nonzero element of a field is a unit, and the pre-Bloch group generated by it would be zero. The intended set is the elements other than 0 and 1, as V.3's own boundary formula requires (the boundary on [x] uses x and 1-x, so x = 1 must be excluded and x = 0 with it). A wording fix in the handoff row, with no change to V.3's mathematics.
